route: No independent-means residence permit found in the IND pages searched (the closest permit type found was medical treatment, which bars work). Once resident, the rule applies. Government.nl: 'You must take out Dutch health insurance within four months of your permanent residence permit coming into force.' The couple is therefore priced as residents under the Zorgverzekeringswet.
policy: Basic health insurance (basisverzekering, Zvw), community-rated flat premium, no health underwriting, mandatory own risk (verplicht eigen risico) EUR 385 per adult in 2026. Cheapest 2026 monthly premium: VinkVink combinatie EUR 142.40 per adult at monthly payment. Wlz (long-term care) is financed through the income tax return, not a separate premium.
working: 2 x 142.40 = 284.80 EUR per month (cheapest). Average premium: 2 x 159.30 = 318.60 EUR per month. The own risk (up to 385 each) is a cost on use and is not in the premium.

eu_citizen_difference: Residents pay the same basic premium. An EU citizen may keep cover from another EU state for a time via EHIC/S1; a non-EU citizen with a Dutch permit must insure within four months. EU citizens can enter without the permit problem noted above.
spot_check: Zorgwijzer gives 142.40 cheapest and 159.30 average, matching Consumentenbond. The government's nominal average is 157, close to 159.30.
uncertainty: The big uncertainty is residence, not price: I found no IND permit for people of independent means, so the NL couple may have no legal route. The cheapest policy is a combined-brand internet policy; it may restrict hospital choice (natura vs restitutie not checked). The own risk adds up to 770 EUR a year per couple if used. Wlz and Zvw income charges depend on how the Dutch tax agent classes the portfolio income. 2027 premiums are higher (cheapest 148.40). Zorgtoeslag excluded by income and assets.
